title: Global Horizons Manpower (Thai farmworkers)
summary: The EEOC alleged that between 2003 and 2007 Beverly Hills-based labor contractor Global Horizons brought Thai men to farms in Hawaii and Washington, charged them high recruitment fees that created insurmountable debt, confiscated passports, and housed them in dilapidated, crowded housing. In 2016 a federal judge in Washington awarded $7,658,500 against Global Horizons, and a companion Hawaii case produced a $12.3 million default judgment. A separate federal criminal case, United States v. Orian, was dismissed in July 2012 after the Justice Department said it could not prove the charged offenses beyond a reasonable doubt.

actions.action: Title VII pattern-or-practice lawsuit filed (Hawaii and Washington)
criminal case United States v. Orian dismissed

journey.note: Thai men were recruited and charged high recruitment fees that created insurmountable debt.
Workers were placed on Hawaii farms including pineapple and coffee operations, where the EEOC alleged passport confiscation and abusive housing.
Workers were placed on Washington orchards (Green Acre Farms, Valley Fruit Orchards).
A federal judge in the Eastern District of Washington awarded $7,658,500 to the EEOC for 67 workers.

lures.quote_or_description: Workers were charged high recruitment fees.
Global Horizons confiscated workers' passports and threatened deportation if they complained; the court gave an enhanced award per worker whose passport was confiscated.
Workers lived in employer-arranged housing infested with rats and insects, dozens to a room, many without beds.
